issue.title: Check sigma_18 to sigma_22 against J for the second zero's 1e-10 need

labels.name: win2
labels.description: Task for win2, the Windows desktop

issue.body:
**What.** Check that σ₁₈…σ₂₂ at ω/ω∞ = 1.09, 1.10 and 1.11 agree to 1e-10 relative between J 1250 and J 1500, at K 45 with 1280 bits. Either run J 1250 at the three nodes, or show from existing files that the J dependence is below 1e-10 there. Recommended by #203's subagent.

**Why.** #203 found that the second zero's crossing needs the σ_n to about 1e-10 relative: 1e-9 noise widens its envelope to 1.0934–1.1005, and 1e-6 moves it to 1.1008. The fit plateaus estimate the σ to ≤ 1.3e-14, but that is the same fit's own estimate. T99's J 1250/J 1500 differences at other ω reach 3e-13 for n = 17–22 (#82).

**Acceptance (can fail).** max |σ_n(J 1250) − σ_n(J 1500)| / |σ_n| for n = 18–22 at each node, against 1e-10. If it exceeds 1e-10, the crossing's uncertainty is recomputed with that noise level.

**Depends on.** #82, #203. It runs on win2 after #204, or on another machine with memory for K 45.

**Results, win2, 2026-11-09 15:35 UTC.** The three nodes of `amp_flint_par.py <wf> 45 1250 1280 --procs 3 --fit phys --mf 6:12 --fit-step 1` (ω/ω∞ = 1.09, 1.10, 1.11, started together at 02:18:40 UTC) ended with exit 0: w 1.09 after 47 402 s (15:28:42), w 1.10 after 47 471 s (15:29:51), w 1.11 after 47 472 s (15:29:52). Python 3.14.10 (`venv-t177`), python-flint 0.9.0 / FLINT 3.6.0, BIOS 3.40, Normal priority, no affinity, no memory guard; products about 7400 s and fits about 39 900 s per node, 0.83 of #82's J 1500 times at the late orders. The J 1500 files of #82 (K 45, 1280 bits, also 3 processes) were run on the old firmware.

**Acceptance: max over n = 18 to 22 of |σ_n(J 1250) − σ_n(J 1500)| / |σ_n| below 1e-10. Met at all three nodes.** `compare_213.py` (exit 0, its selftest ok), from the 20 stored digits of each `sigma_str`, in mpmath at 50 digits:

| node | n 18 | n 19 | n 20 | n 21 | n 22 | **max** | limit / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.09 | 2.72e-16 | 3.73e-16 | 3.20e-15 | 1.16e-14 | 4.07e-14 | **4.07e-14** | 2.5e3 |
| 1.10 | 1.76e-16 | 2.16e-16 | 7.21e-16 | 1.10e-15 | 4.40e-15 | **4.40e-15** | 2.3e4 |
| 1.11 | 1.73e-16 | 4.11e-16 | 6.46e-16 | 4.62e-15 | 1.66e-14 | **1.66e-14** | 6.0e3 |

For context, n = 1 to 8 are equal to all 20 digits at each node (1.09 also at n = 10, 1.11 also at n = 9), and the maximum over n = 7 to 17 is 9.4e-17 (1.09), 1.2e-15 (1.10) and 1.6e-16 (1.11). The differences grow with n. For scale, #82 recorded 1.2e-13 to 3.2e-13 between J 1250 and J 1500 at n = 17 to 22 for ω = 0.99, 1.00 and 1.01 (T99-win2), so the 4e-14 to 4e-15 here are the same size or smaller; this run did not test why.

**What this says, and does not.** At K 45 the J dependence between J 1250 and J 1500 is at most 4.1e-14 relative in σ₁₈ to σ₂₂ at the three nodes, 2.5e3 to 2.3e4 times below the 1e-10 the crossing needs, so the J 1500 values are not limited by J at that level. It is a difference between two J values, not an error bound on either (the `sigma_err` of both J files is `inf`, as in #82, from `fit_info["1_1"]`). Nothing here tests K, or the 1.10 K 45 node's own anomaly (#228 does).

**Controls:** `compare_213.py --selftest` checks that the J 1500 file against itself gives 0 at every n, that one σ₂₀ changed in its 9th significant digit is found at n = 20 and exceeds the limit, and that a 1e-12 relative change stays below it, and that the table's exit code follows (ok).

**CPU, temperature and memory over the run** (the #204 sensor log, 159 readings every 5 minutes from 02:19 to 15:29): utilization averaged 71.7% (Windows processor-utility counter, above 100% over the base clock), package power 112.2 W (33.4 to 194.1 W), the hottest core up to 104 C (TjMax 105 C, 8 readings at 104 C). No crash, WHEA, Kernel-Power 41, BugCheck or Application Error event from the 23:44 UTC watcher restart to 15:30 UTC, nothing was killed.

**Discrepancies:** none new. `sigma_err` is `inf` for both J files, as in #82.

**Raw:** `I213-win2/` at commit 159b2af of choptuik-large-d-raw (the three JSONs, three logs, `exits.txt`, `compare_213.py` and `compare_213.log`, README with the results).

**Recommended tasks:** none from this run. The acceptance is met with a large margin, so no recomputation of the crossing's uncertainty is needed for J.
